blocking_requirement: The registration holds all camera world poses and intrinsics fixed while rotating the robot base about world vertical.
reason: The policy-calibrated wrist camera is a descendant of the robot articulation prim. Every registered nonzero base-yaw candidate therefore changes that camera's world pose. Holding its world pose fixed would require detaching or counter-transforming the camera, which changes the frozen policy sensor/extrinsic contract. Thus no registered 45, 30, or 15 degree candidate can satisfy the intervention definition.
failure_rule_applied: V3-B006 fails closed because no preregistered nonzero yaw can pass all held-fixed requirements. No smaller angle is invented, no camera contract is weakened, and no behavioral queue is generated.
next_command: None under V3-B006. A scientifically distinct future amendment could explicitly permit wrist-camera extrinsics to rotate with the base or replace the intervention with a scene-frame transform, but that would not be this registered experiment.
